objective: Bound parcel policy planning so an oversized batch is refused with a typed input error before any TaskStep or dependency list is constructed, while a batch at the reviewed ceiling keeps the current plan shape and semantics.
decision_supported: Whether the parcel policy planner may accept an unbounded batch, and which parcel count is the reviewed planning budget for a tabletop workstation intake.
acceptance: the planner checks a committed parcel, step and dependency ceiling before constructing any step, and the ceiling is derived from the graph arithmetic rather than from a benchmark host
a batch of exactly MAX_PARCEL_BATCH_PARCELS still produces the current plan shape: 3n steps, n observations, n*n + 2n - 1 dependency links, unique step IDs, and parcel-policy-v3 planner metadata
a batch above the ceiling raises ParcelBatchLimitExceeded with code parcel_batch_too_large, naming the observed parcel count and the limit
the refusal occurs before a single TaskStep is constructed, so the oversized TaskGraph is never allocated
build_parcel_sorting_plan enforces the same ceiling, so the step producer cannot be used to bypass the policy entry point
a regression test demonstrates both the construction the limit removes and the new typed refusal
evidence: focused planner test output covering the admitted 64 parcel batch (192 steps, 4223 links, 140011 JSON bytes), the 65/1000/5000 parcel refusals, and the direct-producer bypass

mutations observed to fail the tests: dropping the policy-planner guard, dropping the step-producer guard, raising the ceiling to 65, making the ceiling effectively unbounded, and widening the comparison by one
pre-fix 100/250/1000 parcel growth measurements: 300/750/3000 steps, 10199/62999/1001999 dependency links, 0.28/1.5/21.7 MiB JSON

post-fix refusal transcript for 65, 1000 and 5000 parcels: each refused with parcel_batch_too_large before any policy decision or TaskStep, at 0.02-1.5 ms of planner time and at most 1.2 MiB traced for the 5000 parcel input
the six committed parcel-intake scenarios still plan 9 steps each with planner parcel-policy-v3, and the parcel evaluation and local-model tests pass unchanged
Ruff check and format output, the Task Packet boundary check, and build/verify.sh reporting no new failures
stop_conditions: the fix would require a distributed or streaming planner
the fix would change semantic actions, routing decisions or verifier meaning
an interfaces schema, libs/contracts model or services/world_model change is required
a reviewed batch size cannot be chosen without inventing one from the benchmark host
a modification outside allowed_paths is required
risks_and_fallbacks: The reviewed ceiling could be wrong for a future intake workstation; fallback is that the ceiling is a single module constant with a documented derivation, so raising it is a reviewed one-line change and never a removal of the check
An unset or removed limit could silently mean unbounded; fallback is that both the policy planner and the step producer call the same guard, so deleting one call is caught by the bypass test

A caller could present a legitimate batch above the ceiling; fallback is that the typed refusal names the observed count and the limit, so the caller can split the batch rather than receive an unbounded graph
Only the parcel step producer is bounded here; other planners build fixed-size graphs and are unchanged
